charts.title: Gross Profit, Operating Income & Net Income
Net Income vs Free Cash Flow vs Company-Defined FCF
charts.annotation: Owner FCF, where shown in the DCF cards, is after SBC, interest income and lease principal. FCF (Alstom-defined) is Alstom's own guided measure, which differs in scope from the OCF-less-CapEx column.

charts.title: Cash vs Total Debt vs Net Interest Paid

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Alstom SA: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash, debt and interest paid
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted). Net interest paid is the actual net cash interest outflow from the cash-flow statement, distinct from the income-statement interest expense/income lines.

For Alstom SA: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses the cash/debt balances at the latest balance-sheet date. Net interest paid rose sharply in FY2024 (€152m) as Bombardier-related debt and higher rates fed through, before easing in FY2025-FY2026.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Net interest paid rising faster than debt (a cost-of-debt signal, not just a leverage one)
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

ebitda.title: EBITDA
ebitda.content:
EBITDA is earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation -- an operating-cash proxy that ignores capital intensity.

For Alstom SA: read it beside CapEx: a business that must reinvest most of its EBITDA is not as cash-generative as the margin suggests.

What to watch:

  • EBITDA margin trend
  • Gap between EBITDA and operating cash flow (working capital)

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Alstom SA: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. FCF (Alstom-defined) is the company's own guided free cash flow measure -- Alstom's FY guidance and investor narrative are framed against this number, and its scope differs from the generic OCF-less-CapEx calculation (it is net of factoring/securitisation movements and other financing-adjacent items Alstom includes in its own definition). Owner FCF (shown in the DCF cards above) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Alstom SA: the company-defined measure swings far more than reported FCF -- deep outflows in FY2021/FY2022 (€-703m/-992m) during the Bombardier Transportation integration, then a recovery to positive territory by FY2025/FY2026. Guidance and covenant language reference this figure, not the generic calculation.

What to watch:

  • Convergence (or persistent gap) between reported FCF and the company-defined measure
  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital and factoring swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Alstom SA: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Alstom SA: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Alstom SA: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Alstom SA: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Alstom SA: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
